tagline: Transparent AI job-search agent for students, job seekers, and companies
problem_statement: AA-35: Autonomous Job-Search & Application Agent — build a personal agent that scans job postings matching a candidate's resume/skills, ranks openings by fit, tailors resume/cover letter per posting, and submits applications with a human review checkpoint.

tech_stack.backend: Next.js API routes (mock JSON data for demo, no real DB needed)
tech_stack.auth: Simple role-based login (mocked, 3 roles, no real password check needed for demo)
tech_stack.notes: Keep everything in ONE Next.js project so it deploys to Vercel in one click. Use mock/sample JSON data files instead of a real database for the hackathon demo.

dashboard_sections: Skill Roadmap & Future Prediction — pick a target domain (e.g. AI/ML, Web Dev, Core Mechanical), show required skills by year (1st to final year), and a simple future-demand prediction chart for that domain
Skill Gap Detector — upload/enter current skills, compare against target-role skill list, show missing skills as a checklist
Career Path Recommendation — suggested roles/companies based on chosen domain and current skill level
Progress Tracker — shows student's learning/application progress as stages with location/status labels (e.g. Skill Building -> Resume Ready -> Applying -> Interview)
Resume/Skill Parser — upload resume, extract skills (mocked parsing result)
Job Fit Scoring — list of sample job postings, each with a % fit score AND an expandable 'why this score' breakdown (matched skills vs missing skills) for transparency
Auto-Tailored Resume/Cover Letter Preview — per job, show a tailored preview with a diff-style highlight of what changed
Human Approval Checkpoint — explicit Approve / Reject buttons before any 'submission' happens; nothing auto-submits without this click
Job Comparison View — select 2-3 jobs side by side, compare on fit score, company stability/job-security signal, growth potential
Application Tracker — table of applied jobs with status and location, plus follow-up reminder dates
Post a Job — simple form to create a job posting
Duplicate & Fake Job Detector — when a new posting is added, flag if it looks like a duplicate of an existing listing or has suspicious/fake patterns (mocked detection logic with a visible reason)
Applicant Pipeline — list of candidates who applied with their fit score, so recruiters see ranked, relevant candidates instead of generic spam applications
Transparency Panel — shows recruiters how the fit-ranking was calculated for each candidate (builds trust, addresses the 'black-box AI' complaint)

cross_cutting_features_to_implement.solves: Existing tools give nearly identical, generic results across every tool
cross_cutting_features_to_implement.how: Every score/recommendation shown in the UI must display the specific reasons behind it (no unexplained black-box numbers) — this is the differentiator vs LazyApply/JobCopilot-style tools

cross_cutting_features_to_implement.solves: Data inconsistency between resume, job posting, and profile data
cross_cutting_features_to_implement.how: Show a small 'data health check' indicator on the resume/profile page (e.g. missing fields, outdated info flagged)

cross_cutting_features_to_implement.solves: Manual intervention pain point — but keep the ONE critical checkpoint (final submission) human-approved so it's trustworthy, not fully blind automation
cross_cutting_features_to_implement.how: Approve/Reject buttons on every tailored application before it moves to 'Applied' status
A simple funnel/progress bar showing where a candidate is getting stuck (e.g. '12 applied, 3 shortlisted, 0 interviewed' — highlight the drop-off stage)

cross_cutting_features_to_implement.solves: Lack of transparency in existing AI hiring tools
cross_cutting_features_to_implement.how: Every AI-generated score or recommendation anywhere in the app has a visible 'why' expandable section

cross_cutting_features_to_implement.solves: Users want automation for repetitive apply actions
cross_cutting_features_to_implement.how: Add a settings toggle 'Auto-scan for new matching jobs every day' that visually represents a background automation workflow (can be mocked/simulated for demo, describe it as powered by an n8n-style workflow engine in the architecture slide)

intentional_demo_bug.purpose: Judges like seeing self-awareness — show ONE small, harmless UI bug live, then explain the real-world problem it represents and how you would fix it post-hackathon. This makes 'Functionality' and 'Presentation' scoring stronger, not weaker.
intentional_demo_bug.suggestion: On the Job Comparison page, when comparing 3 jobs, make the fit-score bar for the 3rd job intentionally NOT update on first click (needs a second click to refresh). During the live demo, click it, point it out calmly, and say: 'This is a real issue we found in testing — async state not refreshing on first render. In production we'd fix this with a proper state-management library. This is exactly the kind of edge case our Functionality testing caught.'
intentional_demo_bug.tone: Confident, not apologetic — frame it as evidence of real testing, not carelessness

screens_to_build: Landing page with 3 role-based login cards (Student / Job Seeker / Company)
Job Fit Score detail page (the transparency 'why' page)
Job Comparison page (contains the intentional demo bug)
sample_data_needed: Generate 8-10 mock job postings, 3 mock student/job-seeker profiles, and 2-3 mock company accounts as static JSON so the whole demo works without a real backend or real user data.
